transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-15
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Reyes (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood Partner Ops); Carlos Mendez (LumenScale Head of Partnerships), Dr. Anika Rao (HPC Solutions Architect), Tobias Klein (Cloud Partnerships), Sofia Petrov (Security)

Summary:
Quick partner intro + discovery call to understand LumenScale's go-to-market, hardware partnerships (they resell GPU hardware + managed infra), integration points (marketplace, APIs), and security/compliance needs. Redwood presented high-level product modes (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private) and discussed pilot/benchmark options. Action items and next steps agreed.

Topics:
- Partner program structure and margins
- Technical integration points: routing, private deployments, VPC peering, KMS
- Benchmarking and pilot: target models, latency/cost targets
- Security and compliance: SOC2, SSO, audit logs

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you all squeezing this in. I'm Maya, AE on the partnerships team at Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Carlos Mendez: Hey Maya, Carlos here from LumenScale, hello everyone.
[00:09] Dr. Anika Rao: Anika here.
[00:11] Jordan Reyes: Jordan, Redwood SE.
[00:12] Tobias Klein: Tobias, partnerships.
[00:13] Priya Singh: Priya, partner ops on Redwood.
[00:14] Sofia Petrov: Sofia, security at LumenScale.
[00:16] Maya Chen: Sweet, thanks. The plan for the next 40-ish minutes is a quick intro from both sides, then technical fit/questions, and then agree next steps. Does that work?
[00:23] Carlos Mendez: Yep, good.

[02:05] Maya Chen: To kick off, quick background on Redwood — developer-first inference platform, we do hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private/vpc on-prem options. We try to make serving predictable across hardware. I'll hand to Jordan to do a quick run of technical highlights.
[02:18] Jordan Reyes: Thanks. So high level: our serving runtime focuses on throughput and latency, continuous batching, KV cache and quantization friendly paths. We support model cataloging, streaming, function calling, and quality monitoring. For partners like you who resell or integrate GPU infra, common flows are — 1) joint offering where you run Dedicated for customers, 2) private deployments for enterprise customers on prem, or 3) referral to our hosted tier for smaller accounts.
[02:47] Tobias Klein: Quick clarifying Q — when you say Dedicated, is that a software-only stack we run, or do you provide images and we operate?
[02:53] Jordan Reyes: Good question. Dedicated is mostly us provisioning reserved capacity in our cloud — but for partner cases we do a 'Redwood Private' option: it's a customer controlled plane, can be VPC deployed or on-prem via appliance. For the partner-managed model we commonly ship an operator image and a control plane connector; details depend on the integration level. The private option has KMS/HSM integrations.
[03:12] Tobias Klein: Ok that helps.

[06:34] Carlos Mendez: From LumenScale's side — we sell GPU racks and also offer managed infra and a marketplace. We're exploring embedding inference runtimes into our stack so customers can buy hardware + Redwood run-time as a bundle. Our goals are margin, a simple onboarding for customers, and a strong security story.
[06:48] Maya Chen: Got it. Are you primarily targeting enterprises or cloud-native startups?
[06:52] Carlos Mendez: Mostly enterprises and mid-market; some large research labs. Typical requirements: SOC2, SSO (SAML), strict network control, and sometimes offline/on-prem installs.
[07:02] Sofia Petrov: And data residency requirements for some EU customers.
[07:05] Maya Chen: Understood. On compliance — Redwood supports SOC2, SSO, audit logs, RBAC, and KMS integrations. For on-prem, we can support an air-gapped deployment with local KMS if needed.
[07:18] Sofia Petrov: Do you have an SOC2 report we can review?
[07:21] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll send the security pack after this call — SOC2 attestation, SOC docs, architecture diagram.

[09:40] Tobias Klein: From the integration perspective: what's the expected network topology for the private deployment? VPC peering only, or can we do direct connect?
[09:48] Jordan Reyes: We support VPC peering and direct connect options; for on-prem there's peered VPN or private link. For partner-managed deployments we typically ask for a peering with restricted CIDR ranges and specific ports — we'll share a checklist.

[12:11] Dr. Anika Rao: Technical Q on performance — what's the expected latency for a 2k token generation on an Llama-2 style open model on a T4 vs A100? Rough numbers to set expectations for customers.
[12:22] Jordan Reyes: Uh, rough ballpark: on A100 family you might see ~150-300ms per chunk depending on batching; on T4 it's higher and variable. Those numbers depend a lot on optimizations — kernel selection, quantization, and request pattern. For production we recommend profiling with real traffic; our Optimize module suggests quantization profiles and batching settings that often reduce cost by 30-60% while staying within latency SLOs.
[12:50] Anika Rao: That makes sense. For our hardware customers, they ask for predictable SLOs — is there an SLA for Dedicated?
[12:57] Maya Chen: We offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets on Dedicated contracts; exact metrics are part of the contract but we can discuss standard SLAs when you want to go to pilot.

[15:30] Carlos Mendez: On GTM — we want clear partner margins and a co-sell model. How do you typically handle pricing for partners who want to resell Dedicated or private deployments?
[15:39] Priya Singh: We have a partner program with tiered discounts and referral credits. For dedicated/reserved capacity we do commit-based pricing. We'll include the partner program deck with details. Margins vary by tier.

[18:05] Tobias Klein: Anything special we need to do to integrate on the marketplace? API hooks, billing integration?
[18:12] Maya Chen: We have API endpoints for usage, usage webhooks, and billing integration options; for marketplace we can provide a white-label flow or deep-link to onboarding. For reseller models we often provide an invoicing integration or we can route billing through the partner — flexible.

[21:45] Sofia Petrov: Security again: is log access available? We need audit logs for customer instances.
[21:51] Jordan Reyes: Yes, we expose audit logs, per-route tracing, and token-level cost/latency breakdowns via Console. For private/on-prem we can ship logs to your SIEM or provide S3 export. We also support encryption of logs at rest via customer KMS keys.

[25:00] Dr. Anika Rao: For the benchmark pilot, what tooling do you use? Do we need to provide datasets?
[25:08] Jordan Reyes: We use a combination of our internal load driver and kube-based runners. Ideally the partner provides representative prompts/traffic. We'll also run a synthetic workload to simulate scale. We typically aim for a 2-4 week pilot for initial benchmarks.

[28:33] Carlos Mendez: A practical question — can the private deployment automatically fallback to hosted if capacity is constrained? Some customers want graceful degradation.
[28:42] Jordan Reyes: Yes, smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variants or hosted endpoints based on policies. That can be part of the deployment configuration.

[31:11] Tobias Klein: Legal/compliance: what's the process for data processing addendum and terms for reseller?
[31:18] Maya Chen: We'll loop legal once we have an MoU; we have templated DPAs and reseller agreements. We'll share the initial docs for review.

[34:02] Carlos Mendez: Anything we should know about hardware compatibility? We sell different GPU types and sometimes customers want mixed clusters.
[34:12] Jordan Reyes: Our runtime supports different architectures but some kernels are optimized for specific hardware; mixed clusters are supported but performance varies. For mixed clusters we recommend model pinning and routing policies to ensure customers hit the right hardware for latency-sensitive workloads. We'll request the exact GPU SKUs so we can advise.

[37:05] Dr. Anika Rao: On quantization — do you have recommended quant levels per model family?
[37:13] Jordan Reyes: Yes, we have quant profiles; our Optimize team can recommend Q4, Q5 depending on model and quality targets. We can run AB tests to compare perplexity/nll and human evals if needed.

[40:30] Maya Chen: Ok, sounds like alignment on the big stuff. Quick recap of next steps: Maya will send partner program deck and security pack; Jordan will schedule a technical deep dive and propose pilot plan; Carlos will share infra diagram and legal contact. Is that accurate?
[40:45] Carlos Mendez: Yes, that's right.
[40:47] Tobias Klein: Works for us.

[43:00] Sofia Petrov: One last small note — can you include contact for SOC2 team in the security pack so our reviewers can email?
[43:07] Maya Chen: Will do.

[45:50] Maya Chen: Great, thanks everyone for your time. We'll follow up with the deck and calendar invites. Talk soon.
[46:00] Carlos Mendez: Thanks all.

Meeting end.
